content:
Liam: Heads-up — after the merge-policy tweak rolled at 12:03 UTC, we’re seeing p95/p99 latency jump on small request workloads. Anyone else?

infra-bot: deploy redwood/serving@release-2026-03-18 merged by @Arjun in infra (rollout: 100%) — config change: batch_merge_min_tokens: 64 -> 32

Arjun: yep that was the change. I reduced min tokens to reduce wait for tiny chats. I didn’t expect the kernel selector to flip though.

Maria: checking kv cache metrics now — miss rate for prefix-cache rose from 6% -> 22% around the same timestamp. Could be evictions from more frequent small batches?

Jonas: p50 unaffected, p95 up ~180ms, p99 up ~420ms on gen endpoints serving short prompts (<= 12 tokens). Throughput down ~8% for that tenant segment. GPU util slightly lower.

Liam: interesting — lower GPU util but worse tail. smells like kernel mismatch + context switching. Any profiler traces?

Arjun: took a quick trace. Kernel chosen flipped from fast-fused-kv (kernel_v2_fused) to kernel_v1_generic for many small batches because batch shapes now more varied. profiler snippet:```
[2026-03-18T12:05:02Z] batch_shapes: {1x8: 48%, 1x2: 30%, 2x4: 22%}
[2026-03-18T12:05:02Z] kernel_selection: kernel_v1_generic (mean 2.4ms/token) -> used for mixed microbatches
[2026-03-18T12:05:02Z] fallback_count: 1345 (prev 72)
```

Maria: KV cache churn log shows more frequent cache invalidation/gc events coinciding with the drop. GC count +3x. Maybe the merging produced more unique prefixes causing cache fragmentation.

Kevin: So two failure modes: (1) kernel chooser picks a slower generic kernel due to inconsistent batch shapes and (2) prefix cache thrashes. Either could explain tail.

SRE Oncall: I’m seeing more tail errors for timeouts too — a few 504s for gen endpoints with 1s deadlines. Can we increase client timeouts temporarily?

Jonas: short term mitigations: revert batch_merge_min_tokens to 64, or add a gating rule that forces fused kernel when low-seq-length fraction > 70%. Which is faster to ship?

Arjun: Revert is fastest. I can push rollback in 5m. But we should log configuration and replay traffic to reproduce offline.

Liam: Agree rollback first. Arjun please revert and post rollout id. After that, let's capture a flamegraph with the mixed shapes so infra can tune kernel selector thresholds.

Arjun: rolling back now -> `deploy redwood/serving@release-2026-03-17 --set batch_merge_min_tokens=64`

infra-bot: rollback started by @Arjun (release-2026-03-17) — 0% -> 100% (ETA ~90s)

Jonas: after ~3mins p99 back down ~90% to previous baseline. KV cache miss rate dropping back toward 7%. Good signal.

Maria: saving GC traces and a diff of prefix keys pre/post. I'll upload to the perf bucket: s3://redwood-perf/kv-churn/2167203456/

Kevin: next steps (assign):
- Arjun: open PR to add kernel selection telemetry (expose batch_shape_histogram + selected_kernel per request) — small change, priority high
- Maria: collect KV prefix samples and GC traces, run a local replay with the merge-policy on to confirm
- Jonas: run synthetic microbench with controlled shape mixes to identify flip threshold
- Liam: write postmortem note in /eng-runtime postmortems if rollout caused visible customer impact

Arjun: PR started -> #infra/1234. I’ll also add a temporary gating rule so selector prefers kernel_v2_fused when >70% single-token shapes.

Liam: thanks. Keep updates here. If rollback does not hold, escalate to incidents.

SRE Oncall: monitoring rule adjusted: alert if p99 > 300ms for > 5m on gen endpoints (was 10m).

Kevin: small note — we should also consider batch_merge_max_variance to avoid highly mixed microbatches. Add to backlog.

Maria: uploaded artifacts and a short notebook for replay: https://internal.redwood/perf/replays/2167203456 (contains metrics, traces, and kernel selection table)

Liam: closing loop: current state = rollback in prod, p99 is stable. Leave thread open for follow-ups and the postmortem. :thumbsup:
